questions.q: If $\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{cotx}{cotx + cosecx}dx = m ( \pi + n ),$ then $mn$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let $I = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{cotx}{cotx + cosecx}dx$
$⇒ I = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{cosx}{cosx + 1}dx$
$⇒ I = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{cosx + 1 - 1}{cosx + 1}dx$
$⇒ I = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{2\cos^{2}\dfrac{x}{2}}\right)dx$
$⇒ I = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{2}se{c}^{2}\dfrac{x}{2}\right)dx$
$⇒ I = {\left(x - tan\dfrac{x}{2}\right)}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}$
$⇒ I = \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - 1\right) - \left(0 - 0\right)$
$⇒ I = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - 1 = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\pi - 2\right)$.

Now using given information $\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{cotx}{cotx + cosecx}dx = m ( \pi + n ),$ clearly $m = \dfrac{1}{2}$ and $n = - 2$.

$⇒ mn = - 1$

questions.q: If& $f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$~be a continuous function satisfying~${∫}_{0}^{\pi2}f\left(sin2x\right)sinxdx + \alpha{∫}_{0}^{\pi4}f\left(cos2x\right)cosxdx = 0$, then the value of~$\alpha$& is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

${∫}_{0}^{\pi2}f\left(sin2x\right)sinxdx + \alpha{∫}_{0}^{\pi4}f\left(cos2x\right)cosxdx = 0$

Now, let~$I = {∫}_{0}^{\pi2}f\left(sin2x\right) . sinxdx$

Now using property~${∫}_a^{b}f\left(x\right) d x = {∫}_a^{c}f\left(x\right) d x + {∫}_c^{b}f\left(x\right) d x$~we get,
$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{\pi4}f\left(sin2x\right)sinxdx + {∫}_{\pi4}^{\pi2}f\left(sin2x\right) . sinxdx$

Now using property~${∫}_a^{b}f\left(x\right) d x = {∫}_a^{b}f\left(a + b - x\right) d x$~we get,

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{\pi4}f\left(cos2x\right)sin\left(\dfrac{π}{4} - x\right)dx + {∫}_{0}^{\pi4}f\left(sin2\left(\dfrac{π}{4} + x\right)\right)sin\left(\dfrac{π}{4} + x\right)dx$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{\pi4}f\left(cos2x\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{2}cosx - \dfrac{1}{2}sinx\right)dx + {∫}_{0}^{\pi4}f\left(cos2x\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{2}cosx + \dfrac{1}{2}sinx\right)dx$
$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{\pi4}f\left(cos2x\right)\left(\sqrt{2}cosx\right)dx$

So, the putting the value of~$I$~in~${∫}_{0}^{\pi2}f\left(sin2x\right)sinxdx + \alpha{∫}_{0}^{\pi4}f\left(cos2x\right)cosxdx = 0$~we get,~$\alpha = - \sqrt{2}$

questions.q:
Let a function $f: \left[0, 5\right] \to R$ be continuous, $f\left(1\right) = 3$ and $F$ be defined as:
$F\left(x\right) = {∫}_{1}^{x}t^{2}g\left(t\right)dt,$ where $g\left(t\right) = {∫}_{1}^{t}f\left(u\right)du .$

Then for the function $F\left(x\right),$ the point $x = 1$ is:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$Given,& $F\left(x\right) = {∫}_{1}^{x}t^{2}g \left(t\right)dt$

By Leibnitz rule we get,~

$F^{'}\left(x\right) = x^{2}g\left(x\right)$~

$⇒ F^{'} \left(1\right) = 1 . g \left(1\right) = 0$~\left(∵ g\left(1\right) = 0\right)$

Now $F^{''} \left($x\right) = 2xg \left($x\right) + x^{2}g^{'}\left($x\right)$

$⇒ F^{''} \left($x\right) = 2xg \left($x\right) + x^{2}f\left($x\right)\left($∵ g^{'}\left($x\right) = f\left($x\right)\right)$

$⇒ F^{''} \left(1\right) = 0 + 1 \times 3$

$⇒ F^{''}\left(1\right) = 3$

$F\left(x\right)$ has~a local minimum at $x = 1$.

$

questions.q: For $0 < a < 1$, the value of the integral ${∫}_{0}^{π}\dfrac{dx}{1 - 2acosx + a^{2}}$ is :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given: $I = {∫}_{0}^{π}\dfrac{dx}{1 - 2acosx + a^{2}} . . . \left(i\right)$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{π}\dfrac{dx}{1 - 2acos \left(\pi - x\right) + a^{2}}

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{π}\dfrac{dx}{1 + 2acosx + a^{2}} . . . \left($ii\right)$

Adding \left($i\right)$ and \left($ii\right)$,

$⇒ 2I = {∫}_{0}^{π}\dfrac{dx}{1 - 2acosx + a^{2}} + {∫}_{0}^{π}\dfrac{dx}{1 + 2acosx + a^{2}}$

$⇒ 2I = {∫}_{0}^{π} \left(\dfrac{1}{1 - 2acosx + a^{2}} + $\dfrac{1}{1 + 2acosx + a^{2}}\right)$dx$

$⇒ 2I = {∫}_{0}^{π}\left(\dfrac{1 + 2acosx + a^{2} + 1 - 2acosx + $a^{2}}{\left($1 + a^{2}\right)2 - \left($2acosx\right)2}\right)dx$

$⇒ 2I = {∫}_{0}^{π}\left(\d$dfrac{2\left(1 + a^{2}\right)}{ \left($1 + a^{2}\right)2 - \left($2acosx\right)2}$\right)dx$

$⇒ 2I = 2{∫}_{0}^{\pi2}\d$dfrac{2\left(1 + a^{2}\right)}{\left(1 + a^{2}\right)2 - 4a^{2}\cos^{2}x}dx$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{\$pi2}\dfrac{2\left(1 + a^{2}\right) \cdot \sec^{2}x}{\left(1 + a^{2}\right)2 \cdot \sec^{2}x - 4a^{2}}$dx$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{\pi2}\d$dfrac{2\left(1 + a^{2}\right) \cdot \sec^{2}x}{\left(1 + a^{2}\right)2 + \left(1 + a^{2}\right)2\tan^{2}x - 4a^{2}}dx$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{\$pi2}\dfrac{2\left(1 + a^{2}\right) \cdot \sec^{2}x}{\left(1 + a^{2} - 2a\right)2 + \left(1 + a^{2}\right)2\tan^{2}x}$dx$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{\pi2}\dfrac{2 $\cdot \left($1 + a^{2}\right)$\cdot {\sec^{2}x}{\left($1 + a^{2}\right)2 $\cdot \tan^{2}$x + \left($1 - a^{2}\right)2}$dx$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{\$pi2}\dfrac{\dfrac{2 \cdot \sec^{2}x}{1 + a^{2}} \cdotdx}{\tan^{2}x + \$left(\dfrac{1 - a^{2}}{1 + a^{2}}\right)$2}

Let, $tanx = t$

$⇒ \sec^{2}xdx = dt$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{2}{1 + a^{2}}{∫}_{0}^{∞}\dfrac{dt}{t^{2} + \left(\dfrac{1 - a^{2}}{1 + a^{2}}\right)2}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{2}{1 + a^{2}} \ttimes$1\left(\dfrac{1 - a^{2}}{1 + a^{2}}\right){\tan^{- 1}t\left(\dfrac{1 - a^{2}}{1 + a^{2}}\right)}_{0}^{∞}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{2}{1 - a^{2}} \left[\tan^{- 1}\left(\infty\right) - \tan^{- 1}\left($0\right)\right]$

$⇒ I = 2 \left(1 - a^{2}\right) \left[\dfrac{π}{2} -0\right]$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{π}{1 - a^{2}}

Let,& $f\left(x\right) = 8sinx - sin2x$

Again integrating with~${∫}_{\pi4}^{\pi3}$

We get,~${∫}_{\pi4}^{\pi4}5 < ∫ \dfrac{f\left(x\right)}{x} < {∫}_{\pi4}^{\pi3}4\sqrt{2}$

$Let $f\left(x\right) = x + \dfrac{a}{{π}^{2} - 4}sinx + \dfrac{b}{{π}^{2} - 4}cosx$, $x \in \mathbb{R}$ be a function which satisfies~$f \left($x\right) = x + {∫}_{0}^{\pi$/ 2}sin \left($x + y\right)f\left($y\right)dy$. Then~\left($a + b\right)$
is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,&

$f\left(x\right) = x + {∫}_{0}^{\pi / 2}sin\left(x + y\right)f\left(y\right)dy$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = x + {∫}_{0}^{\pi / 2}\left(sinxcosy + cosxsiny\right)f\left(y\right)dy$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = x + {∫}_{0}^{\pi / 2} \left( \left($cosyf \left(y\right)dy\right)sinx + $\l$left(sinyf\left($y\right)dy\right)cosx\right)$

And,f\left($x\right) = x + $\dfrac{a}{{π}^{2} - 4}$sinx + $\dfrac{b}{{π}^{2} - 4}$cosx, x \in $\mathbb{R}

On comparing both the equations of~$f ( x )$~we get,

$⇒ $\dfrac{a}{{π}^{2} - 4} = {∫}_{0}^{\pi / 2}$cosyf \left($y\right)dy \ldots \left($1\right)$

$⇒ $\dfrac{b}{{π}^{2} - 4} = {∫}_{0}^{\pi / 2}$sinyf \left(y\right)dy \ldots \left(2\right)$

Adding equation \left(1\right)$ and equation \left(2\right)$~we get,

\dfrac{a + b}{{π}^{2} - 4} = {∫}_{0}^{\pi / 2} \left(siny + cosy\right)f \left($y\right)dy \ldots \left($3\right)$

$∵ {∫}_{0}^{a}f ( x ) d x = {∫}_{0}^{a}f ( a - x ) d x$

$∴ \dfrac{a + b}{{π}^{2} - 4} = {∫}_{0}^{\pi / 2} \left($siny + cosy\right)f $\$left(\dfrac{π}{2} -$y\right)dy \ldots \left(4\right)$

Add equation \left($3\right)$~and equation~ \left(4\right)$~we get,

$\dfrac{2 \left(a + b\right)}${{π}^{2} - 4} = {∫}_{0}^{\pi$/ $2}\left(siny + cosy\$right)\$left(\dfrac{π}{2} + \left(a + b\right){π}^{2} - $4\left($siny + cosy\right)\right)dy$

$⇒ \dfrac{2 \left($a + b\right)}${{π}^{2} - 4} = $\pi + \dfrac{a + b}{{π}^{2} - 4} $\$left(\dfrac{π}{2} +$1\right)$

$⇒ \left(a + b\right) = - 2\pi \left(\pi +2\right)

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
${∫}_{cosx}^{1}t^{2}f\left(t\right)dt = \sin^{3}x + cosx$

On differentiating, we get

$f\left(cosx\right)sinx \cdot \cos^{2}x = 3\sin^{2}xcosx - sinx$

questions.q: $A value of $\alpha$ such that $\mathop{∫}_{α}^{\alpha ++1}\dfrac{dx}{( x + $\alpha ) ($x + $\alpha +$1 )} =lo{g}_{e}  \left(\dfrac{9}{8}\right)$is$

questions.solution:
$I = \mathop{∫}_{\alpha}^{\alpha + 1}\dfrac{dx}{( x + \alpha ) ( x + \alpha + 1 )} =\mathop{∫}_{\alpha}^{\alpha + 1}\left(\dfrac{1}{x + \alpha} – \dfrac{1}{x + \alpha + 1}\right)dx$
Using partial fractions
$= {ln\left|x + \alpha\right| - ln\left|x + \alpha + 1\right|}_{α}^{\alpha + 1}$
$= {ln\left|\dfrac{x + \alpha}{x + \alpha + 1}\right|}_{α}^{\alpha + 1}$
$= ln\left|\dfrac{2\alpha + 1}{2\alpha + 2}\right| - ln\left|\dfrac{2\alpha}{2\alpha + 1}\right|$
$= ln\left|\dfrac{\left(2\alpha + 1\right)2}{\left(2\alpha + 1\right)2 - 1}\right| = ln ⁡ \dfrac{9}{8}$
$⇒ {( 2\alpha + 1 )}^{2} = 9$
$⇒ 2\alpha + 1 = \pm 3$

questions.q: Let $y = f ( x )$ be a thrice differentiable function in $( - 5, 5 )$. Let the tangents to the curve $y = f ( x )$ at $( 1, f ( 1 ) )$ and $( 3, f ( 3 ) )$ make angles $\dfrac{π}{6}$ and $\dfrac{π}{4}$, respectively with positive $x$-axis. If $27{∫}_{1}^{3}\left(\left(f^{'}\left(t\right)\right)2 + 1\right)f^{"}\left(t\right)dt = \alpha + \beta\sqrt{3}$ where $\alpha, \beta$ are integers, then the value of $\alpha + \beta$ equals
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$

Given:

$y = f \left(x\right)$

$⇒ $\dfrac{dy}{dx} =$f^{'} \left(x\right)$

\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)\left(1, f\left(1\right)\right) = f^{'}\left(1\right) = tan\dfrac{π}{6} = \dfrac{1}{3}$

$⇒ f^{'} \left(1\right) = $\dfrac{1}{3} . . .\left(i\right)$

\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)\left($3, $f\left($3\right)\right) = f^{'} \left($3\right) = $tan\dfrac{π}{4} =$1$

$⇒ f^{'}\left($3\right) = 1 . . . \left($ii\right)$

It is given that, $27{∫}_{1}^{3}\left(\left($f^{'}\left($t\right)\right)2 + 1\right)f^{"}\left($t\right)dt = $\alpha + \$beta\sqrt{3}$

Let, $I = {∫}_{1}^{3}\left(\left($f^{'} ( t )\right)2 + 1\right)f^{"}\left($t\right)dt$

Putting, $f^{'} ( t ) = z ⇒ f^{"}\left($t\right)dt = dz$

$z = f^{'} ( 3 ) = 1$

$z = f^{'}\left($1\right) = \dfrac{1}{3}$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{1\ssqrt{3}}^{1}\left(z^{2} + 1\right)dz$

$⇒ I = ${\dfrac{z3}{3} +$+$++z}_{1\sqrt{3}}^{1}$

$⇒ I = \$left(\dfrac{1}{3} +$1\right) - \left(\dfrac{1}{3} \cdot \dfrac{1}{3\sqrt{3}} + \dfrac{1}{3}\right)

$⇒ I = $\dfrac{4}{3} - \dfrac{10}{9\sqrt{3}}

$⇒ I = $\dfrac{4}{3} - \dfrac{10}{27}\sqrt{3}

$⇒ $\alpha + \$beta\sqrt{3} =27 \left(\dfrac{4}{3} - \dfrac{10}{27}\sqrt{3}\right)$

$⇒ \alpha + \$beta\sqrt{3} =$36 - $10\sqrt{3}

$⇒ \alpha =36, \beta = -10$

$⇒ \alpha + \beta =36 - 10$

$⇒ \alpha + \beta =26$

$

questions.q: The value of $k \in \mathrm{N}$ for which the integral $I_n=\int_0^1\left(1-x^k\right)^n d x, n \in \mathbb{N}$, satisfies $147 I_{20}=148 I_{21}$ is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & I_n=\int_0^1\left(1-x^k\right)^n \cdot 1 d x \\ & I_n=\left(1-x^k\right)^n \cdot x-n k \int_0^1\left(1-x^k\right)^{n-1} \cdot x^{k-1} \cdot d x \\ & I_n=n k \int_0^1\left[\left(1-x^k\right)^n-\left(1-x^k\right)^{n-1}\right] d x \\ & I_n=n k I_n-n k I_n \\ & \frac{I_n}{I_{n-1}}=\frac{n k}{n k+1} \\ & \frac{I_{21}}{I_{20}}=\frac{21 k}{1+21 k} \\ & =\frac{147}{148} \Rightarrow k=7\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{2 - xcosx}{2 + xcosx}$ and $g ( x ) = \log_{\mathrm{e}} ⁡ x,$ then the value of the integral $\mathop{∫}_{- \dfrac{π}{4}}^{\pi4}g\left(f\left(x\right)\right)dx$ is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$Given,

$f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{2 - xcosx}{2 + xcosx},g ( x ) = \log_{\mathrm{e}} ⁡ x$

$⇒ g \left(f \left($x\right)\right) = $lo{g}_{e}\left(\dfrac{2 - xcosx}{2 + xcosx}\right)

$⇒ $g\left($f \left(-$x\right)\right) = ⁡ lo{g}_{e} \left(\dfrac{2 - ( - x ) cos ⁡ ( - x )}{2 + ( - x ) cos ⁡ ( - x )}\right)$

$⇒ g \left(f \left(-$x\right)\right) = $\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(\dfrac{2 + xcosx}{2 - xcosx}\right)

$⇒ g \left($f \left(- x\right)\right) = - log\left(\dfrac{2 - xcosx}{2 + xcosx}\right)$

$⇒ g\left(f\left(- x\right)\right) = – g ( f\left(x\right) )$

Hence,~$g ( f\left(x\right) )$~is~an odd function.

By using the property of definite integration, ${∫}_{- a}^{a}f\left(x\right) d x = \left\{\begin{cases}2{∫}_{0}^{a} & f\left(x\right)dx, f \left(-x\right) = f \left($x\right) \\ 0, \text{ and } $f\left(-$x\right) = - $f\left($x\right)\end{cases}\right$, we can write
$\mathop{∫}_{- $\dfrac{π}{4}}^{\pi4}g ( f ( x ) ) dx =0 = \log_{\mathrm{e}} ⁡ 1$

$

questions.q: Let f be a continuous function satisfying& ${∫}_{0}^{t2} \left($f ( x ) + x^{2}\right)dx = \dfrac{4}{3}t^{3}, ∀ t > 0$~. Then~f\left(\dfrac{\pi2}{4}\right) \text{ and } is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$

Given equation is& ${∫}_{0}^{t2}\left(f ( x ) + x^{2}\right)dx = \dfrac{4}{3}t^{3}, ∀ t > 0$

According to Newton Leibnitz theorem we have$\dfrac{d}{d x}\left({∫}_{u \left($x\right)}^{v\left(x\$right)}f\left($t\right) d t\right) = f \left($v \left(x\right)\right)\timesv ' \left(x\right) - f\left(u \left($x\right)\right)\timesu ' \left($x\right)$

Apply Newtons Leibnitz theorem in the given equation.

$⇒ $\l$left(f\left($t^{2}\right) + t^{4}\right)2t - 0 = 4t^{2}$

$⇒ $f\left($t^{2}\right) + t^{4} = 2t$

$⇒ $f\left($x^{2}\right) = - x^{4} + 2x$

$⇒ f ( x ) = - x^{2} + 2\sqrt{x}$

$⇒ $f\left(\dfrac{\pi2}{4}\right) = - \dfrac{\pi4}{42} +$2 $\times \dfrac{π}{2}

$= $\dfrac{- {π}^{4}}{16} + \pi

$= $\pi \left(1 - $\dfrac{\pi3}{16}\right)

Hence this is the correct option.

$

questions.q: If& $n\left(2n + 1\right){∫}_{0}^{1}\left(1 - x^{n}\right)2ndx = 1177{∫}_{0}^{1}\left(1 - x^{n}\right)2n + 1dx$, then~$n \in N$& is equal to _______.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let& ${I}_{1} = {∫}_{0}^{1}\left(1 - x^{n}\right)2ndx$~and~${I}_{2} = {∫}_{0}^{1}\left(1 - x^{n}\right)2n + 1dx$

Now on solving~${I}_{2}$~we get,

${I}_{2} = {∫}_{0}^{1}\left(1 - x^{n}\right)2n + 1 \cdot 1dx$

Now on using by parts integration we get,

$⇒ {I}_{2} = \left(1 - x^{n}\right)2n + 1 . {x}_{0}^{1} - {∫}_{0}^{1}\left(2n + 1\right)\left(1 - x^{n}\right)2n\left(- nx^{n - 1}\right)xdx$

$⇒ {I}_{2} = - n\left(2n + 1\right)\left\{{I}_{2} - {I}_{1}\right\}$~\left\{\text{as}{I}_{1} = {∫}_{0}^{1}\left(1 - x^{n}\right)2ndx\right\}$

$⇒ \left(2n^{2} + n + 1\right){I}_{2} = n\left(2n + 1\right){I}_{1}$

\left\{\text{Given}n\left(2n + 1\right){∫}_{0}^{1}\left(1 - x^{n}\right)2ndx = 1177{∫}_{0}^{1}\left(1 - x^{n}\right)2n + 1dx\right\}$

$⇒ \dfrac{I1}{I2} = \dfrac{2n^{2} + n + 1}{n\left(2n + 1\right)} = \dfrac{1177}{n\left(2n + 1\right)}$

$⇒ 2n^{2} + n - 1176 = 0$

$⇒ n = \dfrac{- 1 \pm \sqrt{1 + 4 \times 2 \times 1176}}{4}$

$⇒ n = \dfrac{- 1 \pm \sqrt{9409}}{4}$

$⇒ n = \dfrac{- 1 \pm 97}{4}$

$⇒ n = 24or\dfrac{- 49}{2}$

But given~$n \in N$~so~$n = 24$

questions.q: Let  \left\{x\right\}$~and~\left[x\right]$~denote the fractional part of $x$~and the greatest integer $\le x$ respectively of a real number $x$. if ${∫}_{0}^{n}\left\{x\right\}dx, {∫}_{0}^{n}\left[x\right]dx$~and~$10\left(n^{2} - n\right), ( n \in N, n > 1 )$ are three consecutive terms of a G.P. then $n& is equal to__$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
${∫}_{0}^{n}\left\{x\right\}dx = n{∫}_{0}^{1}xdx = n{\dfrac{x2}{2}}_{0}^{1} = \dfrac{n}{2}$
and ${∫}_{0}^{n}\left[x\right]dx = {∫}_{0}^{n}\left(x - \left\{x\right\}\right)dx = {\dfrac{x2}{2}}_{0}^{n} - {∫}_{0}^{n}\left\{x\right\}dx = \dfrac{n2}{2} - \dfrac{n}{2}$
Now,~$\dfrac{n}{2}, \dfrac{n^{2} - n}{2}$ and $10 \left(n^{2} - n\right)$ are in Geometric progression

So, \left(\dfrac{n^{2} - n}{2}\right)2 = \dfrac{n}{2} \cdot10 \left(n^{2} - n\right)$
$⇒ $\dfrac{n^{2} ( n - 1{)}^{2}}{4} =$5 . n^{2} ( n - 1 )$
$⇒ n - 1 = 20 ⇒ n = 21$~ \left(∵ n \ne 1\right)$
